request.spec:
A fourth role, restricted, can be assigned. A restricted user sees on the people list only the
people of the crews they lead or belong to (by a person with the user's name) and that person
themselves: no other row is on the screen. Every other figure (the totals row, the header, the
summary, the periods, the pools) is still over everyone on the sheet.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A fourth role, restricted, can be assigned. A restricted user sees on the people list only the
people of the crews they lead or belong to (by a person with the user's name) and that person
themselves: no other row is on the screen. Every other figure (the totals row, the header, the
summary, the periods, the pools) is still over everyone on the sheet.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added the `restricted` role, and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**What a restricted user sees:** the people list shows only the person with the user's name (matched by name or alias) and everyone in the crews that person leads or belongs to. Every other figure — totals row, header, summary, periods, pools — still counts everyone on the sheet. A restricted user with no matching person sees an empty list. The list stays empty until the user's role, crews and aliases have loaded, so hidden rows never flash on screen. If a steward delegation to the user is in force, it overrides the restriction, the same way it already overrides the viewer role.

**Changes:**
- `Role.java`: new `RESTRICTED` value, so "restricted" can be typed in the role form and is stored and audited as `role=restricted`. A misspelled role like "x" is still refused with the error shown.
- `ValidateRoleRequest.java` / `RoleRequest.java`: the error text and comments now list the new role.
- `settings.ts`: "restricted" added to the role choices in the form.
- `PeopleList.tsx`: a new `useShownToUser` hook filters the rows.
- No database change was needed; the existing role column already holds the new value.

**Decisions for you:**
- **What a restricted user can do:** the request only covers what they see, so I made them act as a clerk for permissions and the clerk limit. The tests never have a restricted user change anything, so this is untested.
- **Permission settings:** a permission entry can't name `restricted`; it accepts clerk or steward, as before.
- **Filtering is screen-only:** the server still sends every person to the browser, because the sheet-wide totals are worked out there. A restricted user could still see everyone in the raw data, so this hides rows rather than enforcing access. Enforcing it would mean moving those totals to the server.
